problem.headline: Every enrolment needs a person in the loop
problem.currentState: Currently, there's no self-serve way to use Partner Pack seats. Employees have to find a course in the generic web catalogue and email Scentia to book, with no guide to what they can book or when, so every enrolment needs a person in the loop. Reporting for standard Partner Packs is automated but generic, while premium and qualification Partner Packs rely on Salesforce and Moodle CSV exports that are combined and formatted by hand for each client and sent as attachments. Support queries go to the main public programs queue or straight to the account manager, with no way to answer basic questions and no dedicated place for Partner Pack clients.
problem.strategicAlignment: This supports the Enterprise strategy of becoming a preferred capability partner, moving away from a transactional relationship with our clients. The Partner Pack portal becomes the single place where a client runs their L&D program with us: their employees book courses themselves, and their administrators get full transparency over their contracts and real-time reporting on usage. Tracking usage against each contract's term, flagging contracts that are behind and letting clients renew in the portal should mean fewer contracts lapse. Course requests show where there's demand beyond a client's contract, and online renewal lets clients add points or extend their term. It also frees coordinators from handling bookings and client reports by hand.

solution.futureState: A set of portals backed by Salesforce, with data refreshed every hour. Employees of client organisations sign in with their work email, browse every course, and book the ones their contracts cover, spending from a points balance. Client administrators choose who can use each contract and whether bookings need approval, approve requests, book courses for employees one at a time or in groups using teams, track training progress and points usage, export reports and renew their contracts online. Scentia super admins set up and launch each client, see every client in one place, manage portal settings and administrators, and track renewals. All users sign in with an email link and code; there is no SSO.
keyFeatures: Participant sign-in with work email: contracts start open to anyone with a matching email domain, and client administrators can switch each one to a whitelist (approved list)

Course list showing every course, with ones the employee can't book greyed out and the reason shown, filters (delivery mode, date, category, location, level), points cost, and "few places left" when fewer than 3 remain

Booking with an approval setting for each contract (approval required or book directly), automatic contract selection (whitelist contracts first, then the contract ending soonest), up to 2 requests awaiting approval per employee, and places and points rechecked on submit
Pending requests hold their place and points for up to a month, closing 10 business days before the course starts or when the contract ends
My bookings: status, attendance details, the actual date to cancel by without using points, calendar invites, and a reminder email 3 business days before the course
Change dates or cancel bookings, with points returned if cancelled 10 or more business days before the course starts; date changes stay on the same contract and don't need re-approval
Sessions cancelled by AIM refund their points automatically, whatever the timing, and reschedules move the booking to the new date
Approve or decline booking requests from email or the portal, with reminders and automatic expiry
Client administrators book, change or cancel courses for employees, individually or for several people at once, without approval
Teams of employees, used for group bookings, adding people to approved lists, and filtering progress and exports
Contract view for client administrators: points purchased, used, pending and remaining, usage against time, weekly usage and pace needed, expiry and low-points alerts, FAQs and three key insights
Approved employee list management, including bulk paste with checks, invitations, and single or bulk removal
The primary client administrator promotes and demotes other client administrators
Training progress view, an uneditable points usage log, and CSV exports that replace the manual client reports
Requests for courses outside a contract, grouped by course for client administrators and emailed to the Scentia account manager
Renewals by invoice request or online payment (card or bank transfer), with more points or a 1 to 3 year term
Internal portal: client setup and Go live, client list with usage and problem flags, client details, portal settings, client administrator management, renewals tracking and exports
Super admin list controlled by a single owner, plus a break-glass account for when normal sign-in fails
Salesforce integration to read clients, contracts, courses, places, enrolments and renewal prices, and to write bookings, changes, cancellations, refunds, removals and renewals
Email notification preferences with unsubscribe links

goals: Let employees find and book the courses their contracts cover themselves
Let client administrators arrange training for their people, booking for individuals or whole teams at once
Give client administrators visibility of points usage and employee progress, so they know whether they're getting value from their contracts
Replace the manually prepared client reports with self-serve CSV exports
Avoid gaps in access by flagging contracts 90 days before they end and letting clients renew in the portal
Give super admins one view of every client, without checking Salesforce and Moodle reports
Help clients answer basic questions themselves, with FAQs and support contact details in the portal
nonGoals: Single sign-on - all users sign in with an email link and code
Contract emails to clients (renewal reminders, invoices, receipts) - these are sent and managed by Salesforce, not the portal
Internal Scentia users creating, changing, cancelling or approving bookings - internal booking views are read-only
Changing renewal status in the portal - it only updates from Salesforce
Rolling over unused points - rollovers are arranged with the sales rep and arrive from Salesforce as a new contract
Live data - Salesforce data refreshes every hour, and the portal doesn't show when it was last refreshed
Enforcing course prerequisites - they're shown for information only
Employees choosing which contract a booking uses - the portal assigns it
A dedicated support area for Partner Pack queries - the MVP covers FAQs and support contact details only

milestones.description: User stories signed off; open questions resolved, such as what happens when a booking fails to save to Salesforce and which Salesforce emails already exist
Hourly refresh of clients, contracts, courses, places and enrolments, and writing bookings, changes, cancellations and removals, working in test
Sign-in, course list and filters, booking, My bookings, change or cancel, course requests and email preferences

Contract view, access and approval settings, approval requests, approved employee lists, administrator roles, teams, booking for employees (individually and in bulk), course requests, training progress, points usage log and exports
Super admin list and break-glass account, client setup and Go live, client list and details, portal settings, client administrator management, renewals tracking and exports
Renewal by invoice request and online payment, plus the Salesforce renewal emails
Testing with the super admins and a pilot with one or two clients
Live for all Partner Pack clients

risks.risk: A booking, change or cancellation fails to save to Salesforce, leaving the portal and Salesforce out of sync. How this is handled is still an open question.
risks.mitigation: Define retry and failure handling; show failures with a retry option after bulk actions, and flag them on the internal client list and client details so super admins can resolve them

risks.risk: The Salesforce email automations the portal relies on (renewal reminders, invoice and bank transfer notifications, receipts) don't exist yet
risks.mitigation: Confirm which emails exist in Salesforce early and plan the build of any that are missing

risks.risk: The Salesforce primary contact's email doesn't match any of the client's email domains
risks.mitigation: Flag the client as a problem on the internal portal for a coordinator to fix

risks.risk: Online card payments bring payment security obligations
risks.mitigation: Use a hosted payment provider form so card details are never handled or stored by the portal

risks.risk: Salesforce data refreshes hourly, so places shown can be out of date and a session may fill before a booking is submitted or approved
risks.mitigation: Recheck places and points on submit and on approval, and tell the employee why a booking can't go ahead

risks.risk: Open contracts let anyone with a matching email domain book, including people who have left until their work email stops working
risks.mitigation: Explain open access in the welcome email, and let client administrators switch a contract to a whitelist

risks.risk: Super admins lose access to the internal portal, for example if sign-in emails can't be delivered
risks.mitigation: A break-glass account that doesn't rely on sign-in emails, with alerts on every use and credentials changed after use

dependencies.requirement: Read clients, contracts, course lists, offerings, places, enrolments, renewal status and renewal prices every hour; write bookings, changes, cancellations, refunds, removals and renewals
90-day renewal reminders, invoice request, bank transfer and online renewal notifications, and tax invoices or receipts
Hosted card payments for online renewals
A dedicated email address and securely stored credentials (password plus hardware key or authenticator app), retrievable only by named IT staff

assumptions: All contracts use one points-based model, and Scentia sets the points cost of each course. "Points" is a working term and may change.
An employee can be included in more than one of their organisation's contracts
Business days follow one calendar for all clients: national public holidays plus NSW public holidays
Sessions must start within the contract term; multi-day courses that finish after the contract ends are still allowed
If Salesforce shortens a contract's term, bookings after the new end date are kept, because the points are already spent, and flagged to super admins
Course, place, enrolment, attendance and completion data is available from Salesforce
Renewal prices for different points and terms can be read from Salesforce
